title_pattern.template: What It's Like To [Fight / Survive / Be] The [Superlative] [Creature Group]
title_pattern.notes: Experiential 'what it's like' framing puts the viewer inside the scenario (the video literally shrinks 'you' to bug size and throws you into an arena). 'Deadliest' superlative + plural group promises a ranked roster/listicle (11 challengers) without a number in the title. Channel series format: same title family as 'What It's Like To Fight ...' and 'Turning You Bug Sized' videos. Plain, no caps, no punctuation tricks; curiosity comes from the absurd premise (you vs beetles).

thumbnail.composition: Pure white background, four characters packed edge to edge in a horizontal row: Dumb Doggo mascot riding a blue flying stag-like beetle (left), a giant black Hercules beetle in the centre whose horn pins/lifts the stick-figure hero (eyes wide, sweating), an orange-and-black bombardier beetle (right-centre) blasting a yellow-red flame onto a second, furious stick man (far right). Characters crop off the bottom and right edges, so the frame feels overcrowded and in-motion.
thumbnail.text: None. No words at all; the drawings carry it.
thumbnail.colours: White ground, thick black outlines, flat fills: saturated blue (left beetle), bright lime green (Hercules elytra), orange/tan (bombardier), hot yellow-to-red flame on the right edge. Small red accent of Doggo's collar. Very high contrast, reads at phone size.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Beetles are drawn bigger than the humans: the stick man is head-sized next to a beetle horn, which visualises the premise (you are bug sized). The Hercules horn is the tallest element and the hero's face is placed right on it at frame centre.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Shows three distinct 'deadly' ways to lose (pinned by horn, burnt by spray, beetle-riding dog as boss) = promises variety/roster; the brand mascot is instantly recognisable to 835k subs; recurring stick-man hero in peril with comic face is a cartoon-violence hook that is kid/teen friendly; the flame gives a hot colour corner that pops against YouTube's white/dark UI; no text keeps it clean and title-agnostic.

hook.verbatim_0_to_10s: Hello again, bug sized man. Have you ever wondered what it's like to fight the deadliest beetles in the world? Well, let's find out.
hook.device: Series callback greeting ('Hello again, bug sized man') addressing the viewer as the protagonist; title restated as a 'have you ever wondered' question; instant 'let's find out' with zero preamble. Visually: Doggo zaps the stick man with a magic wand (shrink), cut to POV from the arena floor with giant Doggo looking down over the colosseum stands, then a 2-s roster montage of every beetle we will meet (promise of the full lineup), then straight into a game-show gate reveal 'CHALLENGER 1'. Content starts at 0:10; first fight beat at 0:20.

beats.summary: Greeting + title question + 'let's find out'; shrink gag, arena POV, roster montage of all challengers.
Gate-reveal card 'CHALLENGER 1 / RHINOCEROUS BEETLES' in the sandstone colosseum.
Hercules beetle: longest beetle (7 in), hissing intimidation (hero plays dead), slow on land but can fly (clumsily).
Horn = cephalic + thoracic horns forming a pinch grip; used to grab, hoist and 'suplex you into submission' (anime impact frame).

Subversion: beetle isn't carnivorous, just wants fruit (Doggo feeds banana); other horned beetles shown; 'Into the collection you go' - beetle added to DOGGO'S COLLECTION silhouette grid (recurring progress device).
'Beetle Lore' card; 4-stage life cycle (egg, larva, pupa, adult) as numbered labelled diagrams on a soil cross-section; teases carnivorous larvae 'we'll get to them later'.
Hercules beetle speaks Spanish ('dame un platano, perro'); Mondly used to translate in-story; quiz gag with stick man; 96% off lifetime offer + URL; hard pivot back 'Challenger two'.
Tiger beetle: fastest running insect 5.6 mph = 125 body lengths/s = human at 700 mph (stick man strapped to fighter jet); serrated mandibles; carnivorous.
Beetle charges; it goes blind mid-sprint ('Buffering...' gag) and can't turn - hero escapes... 'Just kidding'.
Tiger beetle larva ambush from burrow, hooked hump anchors it, eats you alive; re-hook via larvae (paying off the earlier tease); added to collection.

Bombardier beetle ('second coolest' - teases a #1): x-ray cross-section of two reservoirs (hydroquinone, hydrogen peroxide), enzyme chamber, exothermic boil, one-way valve, 'butt turret' pulsing like a Gatling gun, 20 shots, 270 deg aim, benzoquinone stink joke.

Diving beetle: arena floods (blue variant of gate card), hero becomes trident merman; bubble scuba tank, paddle legs, tears prey; hero bitten, beetle's stink makes fish spit it out; larva 'water tiger' injects digestive juice.

Diabolical ironclad beetle: naming joke (portrait of entomologist), 39,000x body weight = 500 elephants, survives cars; fused elytra cross-section; lifespan bar chart; RPG radar chart 'tank build'; plays dead -> draw.
Pigeon eats ironclad beetle gag, then 'if you're enjoying the video... hit the like button... Did you do it yet?'
Dung beetle: pulls 1,141x body weight = you pulling a Boeing 737; rollers/tunnelers/dwellers diagram; navigates by sun/moon/Milky Way; king-of-the-hill fight; burrowing owl uses poop as bait.

Titan beetle (biggest, pencil-snapping jaws) - but adults don't eat, larvae never found ('do something pls' scientist gag); you win by waiting till it dies; Goliath beetle aside; 'Can't say the same about the next one' re-hook.

Epomis beetle: hero gets a break, frog is the victim; larva baits frog, dodges and latches on, survives being swallowed; adult cuts frog leg tendons; 'coolest beetle on the list' payoff of earlier tease.
Stag beetles: giraffe stag beetle, threat display, impact-frame back-break; Darwin's beetle treetop flips; reality check - they only pinch.
Imposter (ant nest) beetle as Among Us crewmate in the gate; 'ANT VISION' checklist smell/sound/sight; treated as royalty, eats ant eggs; defends nest with butt spray.

Blister beetles: 'give him a pat' -> blistered hand; cantharidin structure; aposematic colours; eating them = organ failure; Romans thought aphrodisiac (chalkboard gag); kills horses via hay; 'maybe a fight you can win... maybe not'.
Collection complete; 'what kind of beetle are you, Doggo?' - Doggo grows antennae, life-cycle replay as a doggo-grub; frog eats him 'RIP doggo :(' / 'jk :)'; 'See you next time.'

pacing.visual_change_cadence_s: ~2 (almost every 2-s sample differs: host cut-back, photo insert, pose change)
pacing.segment_length_s: each challenger 70-115 s; gate card every ~90 s acts as a re-hook
pacing.joke_interval_s: 10-20 (visual gag or snarky aside roughly every 2-3 sentences)
pacing.notes: Narrated by a single dry, deadpan voice (the 'Doggo' narrator) at a moderate 158 wpm; jokes land on pauses and hard cuts rather than speed. Structure is a strict repeating loop: gate card -> real photo + Doggo presenter -> cartoon fight in arena -> fact/diagram -> twist (not carnivorous / goes blind / plays dead) -> collection grid. Real photos appear for ~2-6 s per species, always paired with the Doggo presenter on white.

techniques_worth_copying: Viewer-as-protagonist premise: 'you' are shrunk and fighting each animal; every fact is reframed as what it would do TO YOU, then a twist on whether you survive.

Game-show/boss-fight framing: numbered 'CHALLENGER N' gate card with the beetle emerging from a dark doorway - a reusable 3-s re-hook asset that marks each segment and promises the list is progressing.
Collection/progress meter: 'DOGGO'S COLLECTION' silhouette grid that fills in after each segment - visible progress, completionist itch, and a payoff at the end ('collection's finally complete').
Explicit ranking teases: 'second coolest beetle on this list' at #3 creates an open loop paid off at #8 ('coolest beetle on the list').
Everyday-scale conversions with a stick-figure proxy: 125 body lengths/s = human at 700 mph strapped to a jet; 39,000x weight = 500 elephants; 1,141x = pulling a Boeing 737.
Twist beats per segment: subvert the threat (it's a vegetarian, it goes blind mid-sprint, adults don't eat, it only pinches) - keeps a 20-min list from feeling repetitive.
Mascot presenter on white as the 'neutral' shot: Doggo stands at right third while a captioned photo or diagram sits left - cheap filler shot that keeps a face on screen.
Game UI overlays: RPG radar stat chart ('tank build'), 'Buffering...' spinner, reload meter, 'ANT VISION' HUD checklist with ticks/crosses.
Anime impact frames (red/white speed burst + shake) for every big hit - one reusable effect.
Cross-section/x-ray diagrams with hand-lettered arrow labels for mechanisms (bombardier chemistry, life cycle in soil).
Sponsor written as a skit inside the story world (beetle speaks Spanish -> translate with the app).
Mid-roll like CTA with a callback joke ('Did you do it yet?') after a segment payoff, not at the start.
Twist outro that turns the mascot into the subject (Doggo becomes a beetle, gets eaten by the frog from an earlier segment, 'jk :)').

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: High. The art is flat-vector cartoon with thick black outlines and flat fills on white or simple sandstone/soil/water backgrounds; motion is mostly cut-based posing, slides, punch-ins and shakes - ideal for Remotion + SVG.
assets_needed: Original mascot presenter SVG (not a dog copy - our own character) with 4-6 poses/expressions, plus a stick-figure 'you' hero with sword/shield, 6+ face expressions (scared, smug, dead x-eyes, sweating, crying)
Parametric bug/animal SVG kit: body segments, legs, antennae, horn/mandible variants, colour fills; ~10-12 species drawn as flat vectors, plus larva/grub
Arena set: colosseum stands (side), top-down ring, gate wall with dark doorway (recolourable: sand, blue/water, smashed)
Background kits: plain white, soil cross-section with tunnels, water gradient, sky
Real photos replaced by stylised 'specimen card' SVGs (illustrated species card with caption + latin name) since we can't use stock photos freely - or use CC-licensed images with attribution
Prop icons: weight 'x N', jet, plane, elephant foot, car, burger, banana, chalkboard, terrarium, phone
components: ChallengerCard (gate reveal with bounce-in title + subtitle, creature slides out of doorway)
CollectionGrid (silhouettes that fill with colour + yellow burst on add)
ScaleComparison (number counter + proxy object + speed lines)
XRayDiagram (masked cut-away with animated fluid fills and arrow labels)
StatRadarChart and BarChart with growing bars
HUD overlays (checklist ticks/crosses, buffering spinner, reload meter)
ImpactFrame (radial speed-burst background + screen shake + freeze)
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Single deadpan TTS narrator at ~155-160 wpm with deliberate pauses before punchlines; SFX library (whoosh, hit, crowd boo, squish, buzz) and light background music; Kokoro/Piper fine.
code_only_remake_requirements.editing_logic: Storyboard as repeating segment template: [gate 3-6 s] -> [presenter+card 4-6 s] -> [arena action 10-20 s] -> [diagram/scale 10-30 s] -> [twist gag 5-10 s] -> [collection 2 s]; cut every 2-4 s; impact frame on each attack verb.
code_only_remake_requirements.length_target: Full format 18-20 min with 10-11 segments; a 6-8 min pilot with 4 challengers would keep the same loop.
